notions.question: How is a business letter laid out in English?
notions.definition: The English business letter follows a standard layout, nowadays most often “full block” (everything aligned to the left, with no paragraph indentation). Order of elements: the sender's letterhead, the date, the recipient's address (inside address), any reference, the salutation, the subject line, the body of the letter, the complimentary close, the signature, name and job title, and a mention of any enclosures (Enc. / Encl.). The date is preferably written with the month in letters to avoid ambiguity: 15 October 2026 (British) or October 15, 2026 (American); 10/03/2026 means 10 March in the United Kingdom but 3 October in the United States.

etapes: Letterhead (company name, address and contact details)
Inside address: recipient's name, job title, company and address
Salutation: Dear Ms Taylor, / Dear Sir or Madam,
Body: short paragraphs, one idea per paragraph
Complimentary close: Yours sincerely, / Yours faithfully,

termes.definition: Line summarising the purpose of the letter.

termes.fr: Présentation à la française en bloc
termes.definition: All elements aligned to the left.

exemple.texte: Loire Valves SA, 12 rue des Carmes, 45000 Orléans, France — 15 October 2026 — Ms Emma Taylor, Purchasing Manager, Midlands Engineering Ltd, Birmingham B1 1AA, United Kingdom — Dear Ms Taylor, — Re: Your enquiry of 10 October — … — Yours sincerely, — Claire Martin, Export Sales Assistant — Enc. Price list

confusions.explication: Writing the month in letters removes any ambiguity.

verification: In what order should the date, the recipient's address and the subject line be placed?

notions.question: Which complimentary close should you choose depending on the salutation?
notions.definition: In British English, the complimentary close depends on the salutation: if you do not know the recipient's name (Dear Sir or Madam, Dear Sirs), you end with “Yours faithfully”; if you do (Dear Mr Brown, Dear Ms Lee), with “Yours sincerely”. In American English, “Sincerely” or “Sincerely yours” is used in both cases, and the salutation is followed by a colon (Dear Mr. Brown:). In an e-mail or an established relationship: “Kind regards”, “Best regards”, “Best wishes”. “Ms” is the neutral form for a woman when her marital status is unknown, or as standard professional usage.

lignes: Dear Mr Smith, / Dear Ms Jones,

fonctionnement.texte: A French-style closing formula (« Je vous prie d'agréer… ») is not translated: replace it with a forward-looking sentence (“We look forward to hearing from you.”) followed by the standard close.

termes.definition: Form of address at the top of a letter.

exemple.texte: “Dear Sir or Madam, We would be grateful if you could send us your latest catalogue. We look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, …”

confusions.explication: A classic British rule, still expected in formal writing.

verification: Which close should you use for a letter beginning “Dear Ms Patel”?

notions.question: How can you be polite and nuanced in business English without being too direct?
notions.definition: The English professional register favours courtesy and softening (hedging): requests are phrased indirectly (Could you…? We would be grateful if…), bad news is softened (Unfortunately, We regret to inform you that…), direct criticism is avoided (It appears that… rather than You made a mistake), and positive phrasing is preferred. The style remains clear and concise (plain English): short sentences, active verbs, no unnecessary jargon. Contractions (we're, don't) are reserved for less formal e-mails.

lignes: Could you please send us the invoice?
It appears that the shipment has not yet arrived.
We would appreciate it if you could consider a discount.
I'm afraid we are unable to accept these terms.
We have experienced some problems with the product.

termes.definition: Level of language used in official writing.

exemple.texte: Instead of “You have not paid invoice 2041”, write: “According to our records, invoice No. 2041 of 15 August remains unpaid. We would be grateful if you could look into this matter.”

confusions.b: French formulas translated word for word
confusions.explication: Long French formulas sound heavy in English: prefer courteous concision.

verification: Rephrase politely: “Give us a better price.”

notions.question: How do you write a request for information or a quotation to a foreign supplier?
notions.definition: The enquiry (British spelling; inquiry in American English) opens the business cycle. It includes: the source of the contact (how you know of the supplier), a brief presentation of your company, the precise request (catalogue, prices, terms of payment and delivery, lead times, quantity discounts, samples), a possible prospect of an order, and a closing formula. It remains concise and precise in order to obtain a usable reply.

lignes: We saw your stand at… / Your name was given to us by…
We are a leading importer of… based in…
Could you please send us your current price list and details of your terms of payment and delivery?
We would also like to know whether you offer quantity discounts / can deliver by…
If your prices are competitive, we may place a substantial order.
We look forward to hearing from you.

termes.definition: Reduction granted for a large order.
Specimen of the product for testing.

exemple.texte: “Dear Sir or Madam, We visited your stand at the Frankfurt Ambiente fair and were impressed by your range of ceramic tableware. We are a chain of 25 kitchenware shops in France. Could you please send us your export price list, together with your terms of payment and delivery times to Orléans? We would also like to know whether you grant quantity discounts. We look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, …”

confusions.explication: An enquiry does not commit the buyer.

verification: What information should you ask for in an export enquiry?

notions.question: How do you reply to an enquiry with an offer or a quotation in English?
notions.definition: The reply to an enquiry thanks the sender for the request and presents the offer or quotation (estimate for an approximate amount): products, unit prices and currency, Incoterm and place, terms of payment, delivery time, discounts, period of validity of the offer, enclosed documents (catalogue, pro forma invoice). It highlights the offer and encourages an order. Legally, a “firm” offer is binding for its period of validity; the phrases “subject to availability” or “without engagement” limit the commitment.

lignes: Thank you for your enquiry of 10 October.
We are pleased to quote as follows: … at €12.50 per unit, FCA Orléans (Incoterms® 2020).
Our terms are payment by bank transfer within 30 days of invoice date.
Delivery can be made within four weeks of receipt of order.
This offer is valid until 30 November 2026.
We are confident that our products will meet your requirements.

termes.definition: Preliminary invoice serving as an offer or as a document for the buyer.
Offer binding the seller during its period of validity.

exemple.texte: “Thank you for your enquiry of 10 October. We are pleased to quote €12.50 per piece for our Vienna dinner plates, FCA Orléans (Incoterms® 2020), for a minimum order of 1,000 pieces. We offer a 5% discount on orders over 5,000 pieces. Payment: 30 days net. This offer is valid until 30 November 2026.”

confusions.explication: An estimate is indicative; a quotation gives a precise figure.

verification: Why should a quotation state the Incoterm and its version?

notions.question: How do you place and confirm an order in English?
notions.definition: The order, often accompanied by a purchase order (PO), accurately restates the offer reference, the items (references, quantities, prices), the Incoterm, the terms of payment, the date and place of delivery, the packing, marking and shipping instructions, and the documents required. The supplier acknowledges receipt (acknowledgement of order), confirms the terms or points out any change (which may amount to a counter-offer) and states the expected shipping date.

lignes: Please find enclosed our order No. 785 for… / We are pleased to place an order for…
Please mark each case… / The goods should be shipped by sea to…
Thank you for your order No. 785, which we are pleased to confirm.
We regret that item 4 is out of stock; we can offer a similar model at…
The goods will be dispatched on… We will send you the shipping documents as soon as…

termes.es: orden de compra / nota de pedido
acuse de recibo / confirmación de pedido

exemple.texte: “Thank you for your quotation of 15 October. Please find enclosed our order No. PO-785 for 3,000 Vienna dinner plates at €12.50 each, FCA Orléans (Incoterms® 2020). Please pack the plates in cartons of 24 and mark them as shown on the attached sheet. Delivery is required by 15 December 2026.”

confusions.a: Ship (to send, whatever the mode of transport)
confusions.explication: “To ship” is also used for consignments sent by road or air.

verification: Why must the acknowledgement point out any change?

notions.question: How do you make a complaint and reply to one in English?
notions.definition: The letter of complaint sets out the facts precisely and without aggressiveness: order reference, the problem found (goods damaged, wrong items, short delivery, late delivery), the consequences, a precise request (replacement, refund, credit note, discount) and a deadline. The reply (adjustment letter) thanks the customer, apologises if the complaint is justified, briefly explains the cause without over-justifying, offers a concrete solution and gives reassurance about the future; if the complaint is unjustified, it declines tactfully and with arguments.

lignes: We are writing to inform you that… / We regret to say that…
Thank you for your letter of… concerning…
On opening the cases, we found that 12 plates were broken.
We apologise for the inconvenience caused.
We must ask you to replace the damaged goods.
We will send replacements immediately at our expense.
We would appreciate a prompt reply.
We have taken steps to ensure this does not happen again.

termes.definition: Quantity delivered lower than the quantity ordered.

exemple.texte: “We are writing about order No. PO-785, delivered on 12 December. On inspection, we found that 120 plates were chipped, owing to inadequate packing. We would be grateful if you could send replacements by the end of the month or issue a credit note for €1,500.”

confusions.explication: “Claim” is more legal or insurance-related; “complaint” is more general.

verification: What are the steps of a good reply to a justified complaint?

notions.question: How do you chase a customer who has not paid without damaging the relationship?
notions.definition: Reminders follow a gradation: the first reminder is courteous and assumes an oversight; the second reminder is firmer, refers to the first and asks for an explanation; the final demand sets a deadline and announces the measures envisaged (suspension of deliveries, late-payment interest, debt collection, legal action). The invoice is enclosed or referred to (invoice number, amount, due date) and payment is made easy (bank details).

lignes: We would like to remind you that invoice No. 2041 for €8,400 was due on 15 September. Perhaps it has been overlooked.
We have not yet received payment despite our letter of… Please let us know if there is any problem.
Unless payment is received within 10 days, we shall be obliged to place the matter in the hands of our solicitors.

termes.definition: Letter reminding the customer of a due date.
Last request before action is taken.

exemple.texte: “Dear Mr Brown, According to our records, invoice No. 2041 dated 15 August for €8,400 remains outstanding. We would be grateful if you could settle this amount at your earliest convenience. If you have already made the payment, please disregard this letter. Yours sincerely, …”

confusions.explication: In a financial context the meaning is “unsettled”.

verification: What is the difference in tone between the first reminder and the final demand?

notions.question: How does a professional e-mail differ from a letter?
notions.definition: A professional e-mail is shorter and often less formal than a letter, but it must still be carefully written. Good practice: a precise, informative subject line; an appropriate salutation (Dear Mr Smith, / Hi John, depending on the relationship); the main message in the first sentence; short paragraphs; a clear request with a deadline; a closing formula (Best regards, Kind regards) and a full signature. Avoid capital letters (perceived as shouting), humour and irony, and informal abbreviations, and check recipients, attachments and tone before sending.

lignes: I am writing to let you know that…
Could you confirm by Friday 20 November whether…?
Please find attached the revised schedule.
Let me know if you have any questions. Best regards,

exemple.texte: Subject: PO-785 – shipment delayed to 18 December. “Dear Ms Taylor, I am writing to inform you that, owing to a production issue, order PO-785 will be shipped on 18 December instead of 15 December. We apologise for any inconvenience. Could you let me know by Friday whether this new date suits you? Best regards, Claire Martin”

confusions.explication: “Attached” for an attached file, “enclosed” for a paper document.

verification: Name four rules for writing an effective professional e-mail.

questions.enonce: Why write “3 October 2026” rather than “03/10/2026” in a letter to an American customer?

choix.texte: Because in the United States 03/10/2026 is read as 10 March
Because it is a legal requirement

questions.enonce: A British letter begins “Dear Sir or Madam”. Which close should you choose?
Which wording is the most appropriate for informing a supplier of a delay?

choix.texte: “It appears that the goods have not yet arrived. Could you please look into this?”

choix.explication: A possible meaning elsewhere (police investigation), but not in business correspondence.

questions.enonce: Which elements must an export quotation specify?

choix.texte: The unit price and the currency

questions.enonce: Which sentence is appropriate for requesting a credit note?

choix.texte: “We would be grateful if you could issue a credit note for the damaged items.”

questions.enonce: Which sentence belongs in a final demand?

choix.texte: “Unless payment is received within ten days, we shall take legal action.”
“We look forward to doing business with you.”

questions.enonce: True or false: in a professional e-mail, you write “Please find attached” for an attached file.

choix.explication: “Enclosed” is used for a paper document.

flashcards.question: Present the layout of a business letter, salutations and complimentary closes, and the rules of register.
flashcards.reponse: Full block: letterhead, date (15 October 2026 / October 15, 2026), inside address, salutation, subject line (Re:), body, complimentary close, signature, Enc. Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully; Dear Ms Lee → Yours sincerely; US: Sincerely; e-mail: Kind/Best regards. Register: courtesy and softening (Could you…, We would be grateful if…, It appears that…, Unfortunately…), plain English, short sentences; no literal translation of French formulas.

flashcards.question: Describe the cycle of business correspondence in English with a key phrase for each stage.
flashcards.reponse: Enquiry: Could you please send us your price list and terms? Offer/quotation: We are pleased to quote… FCA Orléans (Incoterms® 2020), valid until… Order: Please find enclosed our order No… Acknowledgement: Thank you for your order, which we are pleased to confirm. Complaint: On opening the cases, we found that… We would be grateful if you could replace… Reply: We apologise for the inconvenience. Reminder: Invoice No… remains outstanding; final demand: Unless payment is received within…
indispensables: Vocabulary: quotation, purchase order, credit note, outstanding

exercices.titre: Writing a letter of complaint in English
exercices.enonce: On 12 December your company (Loire Kitchenware, Orléans) received order PO-785 from Midlands Ceramics Ltd (Stoke-on-Trent): 3,000 plates, 120 of which were chipped because of inadequate packing. You request replacement before the end of the month or, failing that, a credit note for €1,500. Recipient: Ms Emma Taylor, Sales Manager.

questions.consigne: Write the letter (body, salutation and complimentary close).

criteres: Salutation “Dear Ms Taylor,” and close “Yours sincerely,”
Subject line with the order reference
Clear request with a deadline and an alternative solution (credit note)
Courteous, softened tone; accurate vocabulary (chipped, packing, replacement, credit note)
reponse.corrige:
Dear Ms Taylor,

Re: Order No. PO-785

We received the above order on 12 December. Unfortunately, on unpacking the cartons, we found that 120 of the 3,000 plates were chipped, apparently because of inadequate packing.

We would be grateful if you could send replacements by 31 December, as we need the plates for our January promotion. Should this not be possible, we would ask you to issue a credit note for €1,500.

We look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours sincerely,

Claire Martin
Purchasing Assistant, Loire Kitchenware
